title: a-device-that-surfaces-what-cc-needs-to-know
intention: A device that builds and maintains a typed pattern library for any codebase, and uses it to surface what Claude Code needs to know about X as it works on Y — catching constraint violations before code is written, not after. External cognitive machinery that manages which context is active for CC at the moment it matters — the way temporary working memory, inner narrative, and competing activations manage context in a human brain. The cairn device owns cairn; this device reasons ABOUT cairn, and future projects.
why: Akien verbatim 2026-08-30: 'a huge part of what we've learned is: it does not matter what we do it will be wrong. and what's making it wrong right now is too many things in your head. or not enough. or the wrong things. constantly. there are too many things is part of the problem. the complexity limit. just because yours is higher than aider's doesn't mean it's not there.' Born from CC violating the ground loop boundary 3x in one day — memory doesn't stick (corrected and repeated same day), flags are policy (comment in __init__.py), prebuild steps are task-specific (they answer what's asked, they don't manage ongoing context). This device is physics (Law 4): pattern-match 'Claude is about to do the thing again' and intervene before the code is written. 'So we don't start by trying to build a builder. We start by trying to build a robot we can improve who does things for you. And you and I learn from that.'
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy) — this device IS the physics that replaces the policy of 'remember not to do that.' Also: CP1 (epistemic honesty — the device measures what it claims), I-the-system-is-a-learning-block (the system learns its gates from evidence). Telos aim: the system learns to constrain itself from its own operational history.

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam's invariant pair: proved (Law 3) + feeds-back-to-origin-on-failure (Law 8). PROVE GATE: the tester runs proofs exercising the five capabilities against real code — a hollow proof that the device passes without catching a real violation is the specific Law 8 risk. DURABILITY GATE: git commit + push. WATCHME GATE: emission gate reads the probe spec; see watchme field.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when a pattern violation that would previously have reached code review is caught at challenge time and never written. First milestone: challenge capability catches a known violation type (scope creep onto a completed component) on a real proposed change. WRONG INTENT if: (a) it becomes a linter — deterministic checks belong in sieves, this is for learned/judgment-based patterns; (b) it becomes project-specific — portability to any codebase is load-bearing; (c) it fails to learn from corrections — a static constraint list is not what was designed.
falsifier.horizon: First visible payoff at child-d (challenge prebuild). Full device running when all six children land. The Hex capability assumption (child-c) is the earliest measurement risk — if Hex can't do useful classification, the economics change but the design still works with Claude for digest.

how: Core mechanism: graph tree paths ARE the type system. A component's intention becomes its positive type (what it IS), corrections become negative types (what it ISN'T), proposed changes are type-checked by unification. Six question dimensions seed the initial trees: boundary (where does this thing end), ownership (whose concern does this serve), direction (which way does the dependency point), scope of change (same vs. new responsibility), correction history (what's been pushed back on), and intent alignment (does this serve what the component is FOR). The six core values (CP1-CP6) are the lens — they don't add dimensions, they color every path with WHY a pattern matters. Five capabilities: (1) mine — scan a codebase and derive the initial pattern lattice, cold start; (2) review and learn — take input, identify patterns, learn from corrections; (3) challenge — adversarial check, type-check proposed changes against the library; (4) answer query — what matters about X while working on Y; (5) digest — nighttime/batch mode on Hex, process corrections into updated type definitions, notice which error classes die off. Pre-learning: universal pattern catalog (GOF, SOLID, architectural smells) as vocabulary seeded by LLM. Project-specific patterns from mining + Akien's corrections layer on top. Boris Cherny's constraint approach: make the illegal state unrepresentable, don't detect it after. [ENRICHED 2026-08-31] TWO LABS: this device owns both an intentions lab (the existing congruency lab — compiled positive body, what things ARE and what they're FOR) and a CONSTRAINTS LAB (the mirror — compiled negative body, what things are NOT, what's been tried and burned, what patterns predict mistakes). Same compilation mechanism, mirror bodies. The constraints lab is the standing negative body, as first-class as the intentions folder. DESIGN POSTURE: the device's primary orientation is adversarial BY DEFAULT, not by capability. Everything else in the system was designed opportunity-first (Akien's cognitive style: constraints as the floor, looking for opportunities). This device is constraints-first — the mirror world. Challenge is not a mode, it is the resting state. CONSTRAINT SCHEMA: constraints carry whys — constraint+why, parallel to intention+why. The why does the dedup: digest consolidates incidents with the same why into one weighted constraint, not N copies of a rule. CONSTRAINT PROOFS, three-sided: (1) the founding incident IS the measurement (Law 10 — you looked, you wrote down what you saw), (2) the device catching a live violation is the ongoing proof (the constraint is still real, the device still fires), (3) RETIREMENT — a constraint whose underlying cause is gone is legitimately retired, a state intentions don't have. ALL MISTAKES: not just CC's corrections — Akien's own mistakes feed the same body. The constraint library is about what the SYSTEM has learned is dangerous, not about who was wrong. PREBUILD GAP THIS FILLS: the chart/prebuild pass is task-scoped (it charts THIS build). It doesn't say 'you're about to touch ground_loop, and here are the 14 things you forget every time.' CC's memory has that information but it's passive — not contextualized to what's about to be touched.
